D1_water_source.choice: Rodwell melt extraction of Arcadia excess ice (Hoffman 2016 10 kW / 100 gal/day operating point)
D1_water_source.reason: Owner chose ice extraction over regolith heating; Arcadia excess ice is supported by Bramson 2015 and Mank 2021.

D2_excavator_count.reason: M-WIP Case D2 regolith uses 2 excavators (slides 41–42).

D3_survey_batch.choice: one sol of driving at the published record distance
D3_survey_batch.reason: No published survey-area requirement for this site.

D4_habitat_delivery.choice: Common Habitat assumed landed beside the trench; offload is not modeled
D4_habitat_delivery.reason: Howard 2023 gives no offload time or power.

D5_cost_basis.choice: Perseverance historical cost per landed kg and per operating sol
D5_cost_basis.reason: No published commercial Mars delivery price found.

D6_spending_limit.reason: Accounting only; owner sets any ceiling.

D7_tick.reason: Product pacing, not a physical constant.

D8_power_deployment.choice: Fission power unit deployment modeled as one commissioning job lasting the summed lunar CONOPS durations of Oleson et al. 2022 Table 3.6 (offload 2 d, transport 1 d, control box 10 h, startup 8 h, commissioning 24 h, 1 km cable 2 d = 162 h); no grid power until it completes. Deployment hardware (lander power, rover) is assumed present and not modeled as assets.
D8_power_deployment.reason: Only published deployment timeline found is lunar; Mars durations not published.

D9_rodwell_establishment.choice: Rodwell establishment modeled as a drilling job through 20 m of overburden at the lowest tested rate of penetration (0.35 mm/s, Stolov et al. 2026) = 15.9 h before water production. Drilling power, drilling energy and well start-up melt time are not published. The power draw is recorded as unknown, never as zero: drilling may start only on a commissioned grid with unallocated capacity, its decision is recorded as not physically validated for power, and its energy is recorded as not estimated.
D9_rodwell_establishment.reason: Stolov 2026 gives rate of penetration but not drilling power. Review 2026-11-02: an unpublished draw had been counted as 0 kW.

D10_earth_mars_communications.choice: The Meta agents run onboard at the outpost and act on live conditions without waiting for Earth: their work orders execute on Mars as soon as onboard assurance approves them. The Earth link (live DSN Now, light time, solar conjunction) is context the agents are told about: it decides when Earth can hear from the outpost, never when work can start.
D10_earth_mars_communications.reason: Owner instruction 2026-11-02: autonomous, not remote. The last remote-operations version is tagged remote-final.

D11_dust_and_season.choice: Mars date, season (Ls) and local time come from the Mars24 algorithm at real UTC. A change of season triggers agent replanning. Dust and season apply no rate change: the outpost is fission-powered (NASA: constant power regardless of location, no dust-storm concern) and the package sources publish no dust or frost effect on excavation, drilling or driving rates.
D11_dust_and_season.reason: NASA, Powering Up NASA Human Reach for the Red Planet: "No worries about meeting power demands during the night or long, sunlight-reducing dust storms." No source in sources/ gives a dust or frost rate penalty for these machines.

D12_replacement_logistics.choice: A failed robot is replaced, not repaired: no published robotic repair procedure or duration exists for these machines. The logistics and finance agent orders an identical unit; it launches at the next Earth-Mars Hohmann window (Mars leading Earth by logistics.launch_phase_deg, ERFA positions) and arrives logistics.hohmann_transfer_days later, then is available. Cost = unit mass x cost.landed_usd_per_kg (D5); a unit without published mass (Rodwell) ships with cost not estimated. The fixed-priority benchmark orders automatically.
D12_replacement_logistics.reason: Owner instruction 2026-10-31: implement maintenance, spares and resupply from published data.

D13_orbital_hazard_routing.choice: At genesis the worker searches the USGS HiRISE footprint index for a HiRISE RED product whose footprint contains the mission site and runs SAM 3.1 on it. Only detections in an image that contains the mission site route the survey: boulder and crater boxes, grown by half the rover width (rover.width_m) so the rover centre keeps that clearance, become an obstacle grid; an 8-connected A* route without corner cutting crosses the scene, and the survey drive target is multiplied by route length / straight length. If no hazard-free route exists, the survey is blocked and cannot start. No safety margin beyond the rover footprint is applied (none is published). The route crosses the analysed image; it does not join equipment positions to work sites (no surveyed layout coordinates exist). If no footprint contains the site, SAM runs on the nearest listed product or the reference image, the result is labelled a proxy with its distance from the site, and the survey is not changed.
D13_orbital_hazard_routing.reason: Audit 2026-10-31: detections from an image 600 km from the site were used to approve and lengthen the survey. Evidence must describe the ground it is applied to. Review 2026-11-02: the route cut corners between touching hazards, ignored the rover footprint, and a missing route did not stop the survey.

D14_random_failures.choice: The rover and the excavators can fail while working. Each working tick, a unit fails with probability 1 - exp(-reliability.mobile_robot_failures_per_h x tick hours), from the module failure rates of a JPL-referenced planetary rover reliability model (Stancliff et al. 2005, Table 2). Draws are deterministic per mission, tick and unit (SHA-256), so a run can be reproduced. The fission unit is designed for 10 years without maintenance and does not fail; the Rodwell drill has no published failure rate and does not fail (gap). A failed unit stops its job and is replaced under D12.
D14_random_failures.reason: Owner instruction: equipment failures must be modeled from published data.

D17_user_start.choice: The mission starts only when the operator presses Start (genesis); the API and worker never create it. Start requires the operator token (MISSION_OPERATOR_TOKEN); visitors can only follow the mission and run private experiments. Before Start only the live DSN reading runs. Start creates the public mission once; pressing again changes nothing. A mission recorded under another package or engine version came from a build that is no longer the tool: it is discarded on startup and Start begins a new genesis. Model receipts and spend stay in the append-only event log.
D17_user_start.reason: Owner instruction: the user is the launcher, not Docker. Review 2026-11-02: Start lacked operator authentication, and upgrades advised deleting mission history. Owner 2026-11-02: runs from an earlier build are not kept.

D18_excavator_batteries.choice: Excavators run on their batteries (capacity and energy per kilogram from Schuler et al. 2019) and must be recharged from the fission grid; they start each mission fully charged. Work stops when a battery cannot supply the next step; recharging is decided by the agents (or automatically in the fixed-priority benchmark) and draws grid power. Driving between the work site and the charger is not modeled. The rover is not battery-modeled: it runs on its MMRTG and its published one-sol drive distance already reflects its energy limits; Rodwell and the reactor run on grid or own power.
D18_excavator_batteries.reason: Owner instruction 2026-11-02: agents keep themselves online by managing recharging.

D19_rover_daylight_driving.choice: The survey rover drives only while the sun is above the horizon at the site (sun elevation at the end of the step, Mars24). The published distance per sol (rover.max_drive_m_per_sol) is kept and driven over that simulation sol's daylight steps. At night the rover waits and its job says so; night steps are planned pauses, not shortfalls. The excavators are unchanged (RASSOR 16 h mining / 8 h recharge, D18). Without a mission clock (the offline benchmark) the rule is not applied and the benchmark says so.
D19_rover_daylight_driving.reason: NASA (Perseverance): "the rover needs light for taking images or driving using auto-navigation". Owner instruction 2026-11-02: the agents must account for light.

D20_agent_memory.choice: Agent memory is tiered. Working memory holds each agent's planning cycles, tool results and work outcomes for the current sol. When a sol ends, each agent consolidates its finished sols into at most 24 lessons of at most 300 characters, each citing the recorded cycle, decision or event ids it rests on; uncited lessons are refused, and the consolidated working entries leave the agent's context. The environment package and operator decisions are never part of memory and cannot be changed by the agents. The append-only mission record keeps the complete history, so every lesson can be checked against what happened.
D20_agent_memory.reason: Owner instruction 2026-11-02: long-running autonomy needs bounded memory without losing what was learned (semantic consolidation), and without drift of the core rules.
